text.p: These are the stories making headlines in the Namibian newspapers on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The president of the Democratic Republic of Congo, Laurent Kabila, said at a state banquet held in his honour last night that his country was the victim of an international smear campaign orchestrated by western governments.

- Between 400 and 600 ex-fighters from the People's Liberation Army of Namibia (PLAN) have laid siege to the Swapo head office at Oshakati and are refusing to budge until they have been given the jobs promised to all ex-combatants by president Sam Nujoma last week.

- Meatco abatoir in Windhoek has resumed operations, although negotiations with the Namibia Wholesale and Retail Workers' Union have not yet been concluded. Workers downed tools on Friday demanding higher wages.
- Former combatants protesting in front of the SWAPO offices in Oshakati have vowed to close down all offices in the northern regions if the promises for jobs are not fulfilled immediately.
- The strike at Windhoek's Meatco abatoir is over following an apparent agreement over salary increments of up to 44 percent.
